# Push the agenda to your event app

The person gets their accepted sessions, speakers, tracks and rooms in their event app, with a preview of exactly what goes before it goes and a history of every push. It works for any Sessionboard organization: a self-serve Sessions workspace and a full-platform account use the same tools. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to send an event's accepted sessions, speakers, tracks and rooms one way into their registration or event app (Swoogo today), choose which of the app's events it goes into, see what a push would send, push it, or check past pushes and errors. Triggers on "push the agenda to Swoogo", "send our sessions to Swoogo", "sync speakers to our event app", "which Swoogo event is this linked to?", "link it to the 2027 Swoogo event", "what would the push send?", "did the last push work?", "why was this session skipped?", "push history".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person.
- Scopes: `read:sessions` to read connections, previews and history; `write:sessions` to link and push. A connection limited to particular events is refused.
- Any organization member who can use the event reads; linking and pushing need an organization admin.
- Event ids are numbers from `get_sessions_home` (or `find_event` on a full-platform account). The app id is `swoogo`, the one app available today.
- **Connecting the app is a person's job.** They paste the app's keys on the event's Agenda page (Connections) in Sessionboard. Never ask for keys or passwords.
- Plan: Sessions Starter has no push (Growth adds one app); Growth has one app; more apps and two-way sync are the platform.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write or push.** Before `link_event_connection { action: "link" }` or `push_event_agenda`, show exactly what will happen (the app's event name and id; per kind the counts, sample rows and skips) and get a clear yes in this conversation. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads need no confirmation.
- **Pushing waits for a person in Sessionboard.** `push_event_agenda` writes into the organizer's own app, so it answers `needs_approval` with a URL: say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Do not call it again for the same event.
- **Always preview first** with `preview_event_push`.
- **One way only.** Only accepted sessions and their speakers go. A session that is no longer accepted is removed in the app on the next push. Nothing comes back from the app, and attendee data is never read: say so if asked.
- Linking to a different app event leaves what was already pushed in the old one.
- Words: "agenda", "session", "speaker", "push". Never name the in-product assistant or internal engines.

## The workflow

### 1. Check the connection
`list_event_connections { event_id }`: each app, connected or not, health, the app event it is linked to, the plan's lock, and the last push (sent, unchanged, skipped, errors with reasons).
- Not connected: tell the person to open the event's Agenda page → Connections in Sessionboard and paste the app's keys there. Stop until they have.
- Locked by the plan: say what the plan allows (see Before you start). Do not look for another way.

### 2. Link the app's event
1. `link_event_connection { event_id, app_id: "swoogo", action: "list" }`: the app's events and the one linked now.
2. **Pause:** show the event you will link (name, dates, id) and, if one is linked already, that what was pushed there stays. On yes:
   `link_event_connection { event_id, app_id: "swoogo", action: "link", remote_event_id }`.

### 3. Preview
`preview_event_push { event_id, app_id: "swoogo" }`: per kind (sessions, speakers, tracks, rooms) the count, sample rows in the app's own field names, and what is skipped and why. It reads Sessionboard only and works before connecting. Before the event is linked to an app event, every row comes back skipped with "Missing event_id" (`code: "remote_event"`): that is expected. Say the rows are ready and that linking (step 2) is what's missing, not that the sessions are wrong.
**Pause:** show the counts, a few sample rows, and every skip with its reason. Offer to fix skips first (for example a session with no time: the `build-the-agenda` skill; a speaker with no email: `get-speakers-ready`). Ask "Push this to Swoogo?"

### 4. Push
On yes: `push_event_agenda { event_id, app_id: "swoogo", asked }` (pass the person's words in `asked`). It answers `needs_approval`: say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. After a person approves, only what changed is sent. If a push is already running, the answer says so: wait and read the history.

### 5. Check the result
`get_push_history { event_id, app_id: "swoogo" }`: every push, newest first (up to 100): when, who, result, and sent / unchanged / skipped / errors per kind with reasons. Lead with the latest result and any errors in plain words, then what to fix before pushing again.

## When something goes wrong

- "Pushing the agenda to another app is part of Sessions Growth." (`plan_limit`): the Starter plan has no push. Nothing changed. A person with admin rights chooses Growth in Sessions → Plan and billing.
- 403 "Two-way integrations is not part of this Sessions plan" (`enterprise_only`): a second app on Growth. It is the platform.
- `trial_ended` / `plan_ended`: read-only. History and previews can still be read.
- 403 "Forbidden … read:sessions …": missing scope or not an organization admin. Reconnect if scopes were added later.
- 404: check the event id with `get_sessions_home`. 400 "remote_event_id is required to link": list the app's events first.
- Errors inside a push (in the history) come with the app's reason: say it as written and what in Sessionboard would fix it.

## What this skill does not do

- Cannot connect or disconnect the app, or take its keys (a person does it on the Agenda page).
- The push supports Swoogo. If the person names Cvent or Bizzabo, say the push works with Swoogo only.
- No two-way sync, no pulling sessions or attendees back, no scheduled automatic pushes.
- Pushes only accepted sessions and their speakers; no sponsors, submissions or custom fields.

## Tools used

- `get_sessions_home` — Sessions events (read)
- `find_event` — find a full-platform event by name (read)
- `list_event_connections` — apps, health, linked event, plan lock, last push (read)
- `link_event_connection` — list the app's events, or link one (`list` reads; `link` writes)
- `preview_event_push` — what one push would send, in the app's fields (read)
- `push_event_agenda` — push accepted sessions, speakers, tracks and rooms (writes to the app; waits in Sessionboard)
- `get_push_history` — every push with counts, skips and errors (read)

skills.instructions:
# Registration pacing check

The person gets one short pacing brief for an event: where registrations stand, an estimate of where they will land, how that compares with the goal or last time, where the funnel leaks, capacity and waitlist pressure, and up to three next moves. On the day, it adds check-in progress. It works for any Sessionboard organization, full-platform or self-serve, with the same tools; parts the org's plan or event does not have are skipped and said. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you. Nothing is changed or sent.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to know whether an event's registrations are on pace — registrations so far, the estimate at the event date, pace against the goal, where the registration funnel leaks, what is selling out, how long the waitlist is, and on the day who has checked in — with a few suggested next moves. Read-only; sends nothing. Triggers on "are we on pace?", "how are registrations tracking?", "will we hit 600?", "how many will show up?", "where are people dropping off in checkout?", "what's selling out?", "how long is the waitlist?", "who's checked in so far?", "give me the door list".

## Before you start

- The person is connected to the Sessionboard connector, signed in with OAuth as themselves.
- Scopes: `read:registrations` (a preview scope, granted only when named) for the Registration reads; `read:marketing` for the estimate (`get_turnout`) and the in-person door list (`whos_coming`, `check_in_list`); `read:events` for Advocacy pacing.
- Sessionboard checks the event: Registration must be switched on for it (Early Access, per event); the estimate needs an org plan that includes Marketing; the door list is for in-person (field) events. The person must reach the event: an OAuth connection reaches events where their role has AI Access ("Can access AI tools").

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Read-only. Suggest, never act.** Every tool here reads. Offer next moves in words. Acting on one (an email, a campaign, ads, a price change) is a separate request that needs its own clear yes in this conversation, through tools that are not part of this skill.
- **Confirm before every write or send.** There are none here. Never infer a yes for a later write from this check.
- **Some actions wait for a person in Sessionboard.** No tool here answers `needs_approval`. If one ever returns "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>", pass it on and stop.
- **Estimates are estimates.** Every number in `get_turnout`'s `prediction` is an estimate: say "about" and "estimate", give the `range` and `confidence`, and quote `prediction.how` when asked. With `insufficient_history` or `too_early` there is no number: say so and never make one up.
- **Label every number with where it came from** (registration summary, estimate, funnel, capacity, waitlist, Advocacy, door list).
- **Personal data is real and unmasked.** Ask before listing names or emails (for example, who has not checked in).
- **Money is in cents.** Divide by 100 and give the currency.
- **Words.** Say **attendee**, **waitlist**, **check-in**, **Advocacy** (people sharing the event). Never name internal engines or the in-product assistant.

## The workflow

### 1. Pick the event
1. `find_event { search }` (or `list_events {}`). **Pause:** if several match, ask which one.
2. Note whether it is a conference with Registration or an in-person field event. A field event's id also works for `whos_coming` and `check_in_list`.

### 2. Where registrations stand
1. `read_registration_summary { event_id }`. Take registrations by status (confirmed, pending approval, waitlisted, checked in; canceled is never counted as registered), registrations per day, per ticket type, revenue and invoices owed.
2. A 403 "not enabled for this event" means Registration is off: skip steps 2, 4, 5 and 6 and say so. Continue with the estimate.

### 3. The estimate and the goal
1. `get_turnout { event_id }`. Here `event_id` is a number. Without it, the next upcoming event is used: confirm that is the one.
2. Lead with `summary`. Then `prediction` (estimate, range, confidence), `pace.line` (ahead, on track, behind, reached, missed) and `last_edition`.
3. `goal.default: true` means nobody set a goal and it is last time's numbers: say "against last time's numbers".
4. Keep up to three `suggestions`; each `ask` is the request that would act on it. Do not run it.
5. A 403 that mentions Marketing means the org's plan does not include it. Leave the estimate out and say why. Do not compute your own.

### 4. Where the funnel leaks
- `read_registration_funnel { event_id }`. Per form: views → checkouts started → completed → registered, with conversion and abandonment rates. Name the weakest form, abandoned checkouts and their value, and abandonment over the last 7 and 30 days. Read `definitions` before explaining a count.

### 5. Capacity
- `read_registration_capacity { event_id }`. Name what is sold out or above 90% full, and shared pools with percent full.

### 6. Waitlist
- `read_registration_waitlist { event_id }`. Total waiting, the oldest wait, open and expired offers, and whether each form auto-promotes.

### 7. Optional: sharing pace against last year
- If the event uses Advocacy: `find_event { search }` for last year's edition, then `get_advocacy_pacing { event_id, compare_event_id }`. Give `to_date` and `change_vs_compare`.

### 8. On the day: check-in
- Conference with Registration: the checked-in count is in `read_registration_summary`. **Pause:** ask before listing people. For names: `find_registrations { action: "search", event_id, status: ["confirmed"] }` (confirmed, not yet checked in).
- In-person field event: `whos_coming { eventId }` for counts (registered, approved, waitlisted, checked in, plus-ones, seats left); `check_in_list { eventId }` for the door list A–Z. `eventId` is the number.

### 9. Write the brief

```
<Event> — pacing on <date>
Headline: <on pace / behind / ahead>, in one sentence (estimate)
Registered so far: N confirmed, N pending, N waitlisted (registration summary)
Estimate at the event date: about N (range A–B, confidence) (estimate)
Against the goal: <pace line> (estimate)
Funnel: weakest form, abandonment (funnel)
Capacity: sold out / nearly full (capacity)
Waitlist: N waiting, oldest N days (waitlist)
Next moves: up to 3, each one line, each "not done"
```

**Pause:** end by asking which next move, if any, they want to take on. Do not start it here.

## When something goes wrong

- 403 "… is not enabled for this event": Registration is off for the event. Skip those parts; do not retry.
- 403 "… needs the read:registrations scope": reconnect with the scope, or get AI Access on the event.
- 403 "This token cannot use Marketing …": no `read:marketing` scope, or the plan has no Marketing. Skip the estimate and door list.
- 403 "Reading Advocacy results needs the read:events scope": skip Advocacy pacing.
- 404 "Not found …": check the event id with `find_event`.
- `prediction.status` `insufficient_history`, `too_early` or `no_date`: no estimate. Say it in the person's terms.

## What this skill does not do

- Send reminders, launch campaigns or ads, change prices, capacity or the goal.
- Check anyone in or promote from the waitlist.
- Forecast without `get_turnout`: there is no other estimate, and you must not make one.
- Day-of check-in times per person for conferences (no check-in list tool for Registration).

## Tools used

- `find_event` — find the event and last year's edition (read)
- `list_events` — list events when none is named (read)
- `read_registration_summary` — registrations by status, day, ticket; revenue (read)
- `get_turnout` — the estimate, pace against the goal, suggestions (read)
- `read_registration_funnel` — conversion and abandonment per form (read)
- `read_registration_capacity` — sold out and nearly full (read)
- `read_registration_waitlist` — waitlist size and offers (read)
- `get_advocacy_pacing` — sharing activity against another edition (read)
- `find_registrations` — confirmed attendees not yet checked in (read)
- `whos_coming` — in-person event counts and guest list (read)
- `check_in_list` — in-person event door list (read)

# Review submissions and decide

The person gets a clear view of every submission with their team's picks, records their own decisions (accept, waitlist, decline), and tells declined and waitlisted speakers with an email they have seen first. It works for any Sessionboard organization: a self-serve Sessions workspace and a full-platform account use the same tools. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to go through an event's submissions, see what their team thinks, record their own pick, accept, waitlist or decline sessions, and tell speakers the outcome with the decision emails (preview, edit, send). Triggers on "what came in for the summit?", "show me the undecided submissions", "what did the team think of this one?", "put me down as a yes on the AI panel", "accept these five", "waitlist the workshop", "decline the rest", "how many speakers can we still accept?", "show me the decline email", "make the waitlist email warmer", "tell the declined speakers".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person.
- Reading needs `read:sessions`; picks, decisions and email changes need `write:sessions`. A connection limited to particular events is refused.
- Any organization member who can use the event reads. Picks, decisions, and editing or sending emails need an organization admin. A role that sees only some contacts is refused here.
- Event ids are numbers from `get_sessions_home` (or `find_event` on a full-platform account). Session ids come from `list_submissions`.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write or send.** Before `set_my_pick`, `decide_submission`, `update_decision_email` or `send_decision_emails`, show exactly what will change (each session title and its new decision, the email text, how many speakers) and get a clear yes in this conversation. One yes can cover a list you showed item by item; anything not on that list needs its own yes. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads need no confirmation.
- **The person decides.** Summarize submissions and picks; do not pick or decide on your own judgement. When the person asks for "the strongest" or "the best few" and there are no team picks to go on, show the candidates and ask which ones. A teammate's pick is never yours to set: `set_my_pick` sets only the signed-in person's own pick.

- **Deciding sends no email.** Accepted speakers hear through Sessionboard's Speaker emails invite. Declined and waitlisted speakers are told only with `send_decision_emails`.
- **Sending waits for a person in Sessionboard.** `send_decision_emails` answers `needs_approval` with a URL: say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Do not call it again for the same event and kind.
- Always preview the email with `preview_decision_email` before asking to send.
- Words: committee scoring is **Review** (Review plan, Reviewer, Round). Never say "evaluation", "evaluator" or "judge". Say accept / decline, never approve / reject. Never name the in-product assistant or internal engines.
- Committee Review with Review plans, Reviewers and Rounds is the Sessionboard platform; these tools do not run it. Team picks are the lightweight team signal.

## The workflow

### 1. See what came in
1. `get_sessions_home {}`: each event's counts (submitted, undecided, accepted, declined).
2. `list_submissions { event_id, view?, status? }`. `view: "submissions"` keeps what came through the call; `status` is pending (undecided), accepted, waitlisted or declined. Each session has its speakers, description, decision, `track_id`, the team's tally (`picks`: yes, maybe, no, and the person's own pick), and `answers` to the call's own questions, per session and per speaker.
3. The list gives only `track_id`: read the track names once from `get_sessions_event { event_id }` (its tracks list) and show names, never ids.
4. Show a short table: title, speakers, track, tally, decision. Offer to go one by one or by track, and quote a submission's answers when the person asks about one.

### 2. Read the team's picks on one submission
`get_team_picks { event_id, session_id }`: each teammate's Yes / Maybe / No with their comment, and the tally. Quote comments as written.

### 3. Record the person's own pick
**Pause:** "Put you down as <yes|maybe|no> on '<title>'<, with the comment '…'>?" On yes:
`set_my_pick { event_id, session_id, pick, comment? }`. `pick: "clear"` removes it; an empty comment clears the comment.

### 4. Decide
1. Before accepting, check room: `list_event_speakers { event_id }` gives the event's speakers with their `sessions` and the plan's `limit` for the event. It also lists speakers linked to the event with no accepted session (`sessions: []`, for example on undecided submissions): count only speakers with at least one session against `limit`. Accepting past it is refused.
2. **Pause:** list each session title with its new decision (accept, waitlist, decline or undecided) and say "No email goes out from this step." Ask for a yes.
3. One call per session: `decide_submission { event_id, session_id, decision }`. Accepted sessions go on the agenda and their speakers onto Speakers.
4. Report what changed and anything refused.

### 5. Decision emails
1. `get_decision_emails { event_id }`: the accepted email (Sessionboard's Speaker emails invite), the declined and waitlisted templates, the merge fields (`{first_name}`, `{session_title}`, `{event_name}`, `{event_dates}`, `{organization}` …) and how many speakers in each decision have not been told yet. `waiting.accepted` stays 0 after accepting: accepted speakers are told through the Speaker emails invite in Sessionboard, not counted here.
2. Preview: `preview_decision_email { event_id, kind, subject?, body?, session_id? }` shows the email exactly as a speaker gets it. Pass `subject` / `body` to preview a draft before saving. `kind` is accepted, declined or waitlisted.
3. To change the declined or waitlisted email: draft the text, preview it, then **Pause:** show subject and body. On yes: `update_decision_email { event_id, kind, subject, body }`. Both are required and both are replaced: send the current value of the one you keep. Empty subject and body put the default back. The accepted email is edited in Sessionboard (Speakers), not here.
4. To send: **Pause:** show the preview and say "This emails N <declined|waitlisted> speakers who have not been told (or only the sessions you named). Each gets it once. Send?" On yes:
   `send_decision_emails { event_id, kind, session_ids?, asked }`. Leave out `session_ids` for everyone not yet told; never send an empty list.
   - `needs_approval`: "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>". Stop.
   - `nothing_to_send`: everyone in that decision has already had it; nothing was sent.
5. Unsubscribed and bounced addresses are skipped.

## When something goes wrong

- 403 "More speakers on this event is not part of this Sessions plan" (`enterprise_only`): accepting would pass the plan's speakers. Nothing changed. A person with admin rights can choose a bigger plan in Sessions → Plan and billing.
- 403 about committee review (`review_plans`): Review plans are the platform.
- `trial_ended` / `plan_ended`: read-only. Everything can still be read.
- 403 "Forbidden … needs the read:sessions scope …": missing scope or not an organization admin. Reconnect if scopes were added later.
- 404: check the event id (`get_sessions_home`) and session ids (`list_submissions`). Team picks exist only on Sessions events.
- 400 / 409 with a message: say the message; read the list again before retrying.

## What this skill does not do

- No committee Review: no Review plans, Reviewer assignments, Rounds or scores.
- No pick or comment on a teammate's behalf.
- Cannot edit or send the accepted email (Sessionboard's Speaker emails invite, edited and sent there).
- No scheduled sends; no email to accepted speakers from here.

## Tools used

- `get_sessions_home` — events and their decision counts (read)
- `find_event` — find a full-platform event by name (read)
- `list_submissions` — submissions with speakers, decision, team tally and answers (read)
- `get_sessions_event` — the event's track names for the table (read)
- `get_team_picks` — each teammate's pick and comment on one submission (read)
- `set_my_pick` — the person's own Yes / Maybe / No and comment (write)
- `list_event_speakers` — accepted speakers and the plan's speaker limit (read)
- `decide_submission` — accept, waitlist, decline or undecided; sends nothing (write)
- `get_decision_emails` — the three emails, merge fields, who has not been told (read)
- `preview_decision_email` — one email exactly as a speaker gets it (read)
- `update_decision_email` — save the declined or waitlisted email (write)
- `send_decision_emails` — email declined or waitlisted speakers (sends; waits in Sessionboard)

skills.instructions:
# Run your call for speakers

The person gets a call for speakers (the event's submission form) that says what they want, asks the questions they need, opens on their OK, and a running view of what has come in. It works for any Sessionboard organization: a self-serve Sessions workspace and a full-platform account use the same tools. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to set up, open, edit, extend or close the call for speakers for an event, change the questions speakers answer, set the tracks and formats speakers pick from, or see what has come in. Triggers on "open our call for speakers", "set up the CFP for the summit", "change the welcome text", "add a question about audience level", "make the bio required", "extend the deadline to March 1", "close submissions", "what's the link to submit?", "how many submissions so far?", "any new proposals this week?", "enter this proposal someone emailed me".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person.
- Reading needs the `read:sessions` scope; changes need `write:sessions`. A connection limited to particular events is refused; it needs an organization-wide connection.
- Any organization member who can use the event can read. Changing the call, its questions and lists needs an organization admin. A role that sees only some contacts is refused here and uses the event's Sessions pages instead.
- Event ids here are numbers. `get_sessions_home` lists the Sessions events; on a full-platform account `find_event` or `list_events` also give the id.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write.** Before `manage_sessions_event`, `manage_call_for_speakers`, `manage_call_questions`, `set_rooms_and_tracks` or `manage_program_session`, show exactly what will change (the text, the date, the question, the full list) and get a clear yes in this conversation. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads need no confirmation.
- **Opening the call waits for a person in Sessionboard.** `manage_call_for_speakers { action: "open" }` answers `needs_approval` with a URL. Say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Do not call it again for the same event.
- **Question changes are live at once.** They reach the public form immediately; nothing is emailed. Removing a question keeps the answers already given: say how many (`answered`) before you remove it.
- Title, Description, First name, Last name and Email are always asked and always required (`locked`). Do not try to remove them or make them optional.
- Conditional questions (shown only after a certain answer), a second form, submission fees and committee Review (Review plans, Reviewers, Rounds) are the Sessionboard platform. Say so; do not try another way.
- Speakers who submit get a confirmation email. Decisions are emailed only through the review skill's decision emails.
- Words: say "call for speakers" or "submission form", "submission", "accept / decline". Never "evaluation", "evaluator" or "judge". Never name the in-product assistant or internal engines.

## The workflow

### 1. Find or create the event
1. `get_sessions_home {}`: the plan, every Sessions event with its counts and whether its call is open. It lists Sessions events only, so on a full-platform account an empty list is normal: `find_event { search }` finds the event by name.
2. If there is no event yet: **Pause:** show the name, start and end (date and time; if the person gives only days, propose 09:00 to 17:00 on the event's clock and ask), timezone (IANA, e.g. America/Chicago), where, and the language speakers will read (en, fr, de or es). Ask "Create this event?" On yes: `manage_sessions_event { action: "create", name, start_date?, end_date?, timezone?, location?, language? }`. `start_date` and `end_date` are ISO date-times with an offset (`2027-05-12T09:00:00-05:00`); a bare day is refused. A new event comes with a closed call, a few rooms and tracks, and an empty agenda. If the result says the language update failed, the event exists: retry only `manage_sessions_event { action: "update", event_id, language }`, never create it again.

### 2. Read the call as speakers see it
`get_sessions_event { event_id }`: the call is in `event.cfp`: `welcome_title`, `welcome_description`, `close_at`, `is_open` and `url` (the public link), plus tracks, formats, rooms and counts. Show the person the title, the welcome text and the closing date. In step 3 these are written as `title` (from `welcome_title`), `welcome_text` (from `welcome_description`) and `closes_at` (from `close_at`).

### 3. Change the wording or the closing date
**Pause:** show the new title, welcome text (plain text, blank lines between paragraphs) and closing date. On yes:
`manage_call_for_speakers { action: "update", event_id, title?, welcome_text?, closes_at? }`
- `closes_at` as a day (`2027-03-01`) closes at the end of that day on the event's clock; an ISO time with offset closes at that moment; `""` clears it.
- To extend a deadline, this is the same call with a later `closes_at`.

### 4. Set the questions
1. `get_call_questions { event_id }`: two groups in form order, `session` (About the session) and `speaker` (About the speaker). Each question has `field_id`, `label`, `kind`, `is_required`, `locked`, `answered`, and for choice questions `options` (each `{ id, label }`). `catalog` lists fields each group can still add, each with its `type` and `options`. `limits.custom_questions` is `{ max, used }`: how many questions of its own the plan allows and how many are in use (`max: null` = no limit).
2. Pick the change, show it, ask, then call `manage_call_questions` once per change. Before creating a question, look in `catalog` for a ready-made field that already asks it (for example "Level" for audience level) and offer that first: it uses none of the plan's own questions and matches the platform's reports.
   - Add a ready-made field: `{ action: "add", event_id, field_id, required? }` (field from `catalog`).
   - A new question: `{ action: "create", event_id, group, label, kind, choices?, required? }`. `kind` is short_text, long_text, single_choice, multiple_choice, yes_no, link or number; choices only for the two choice kinds.
   - Remove: `{ action: "remove", event_id, field_id }`. **Pause:** "N speakers already answered this; their answers stay stored. Remove it?"
   - Required or optional: `{ action: "set_required", event_id, field_id, required }`.
   - Reorder: `{ action: "reorder", event_id, group, field_ids }` with every question of that group exactly once.
3. Read `get_call_questions` again and show the result.

### 5. Tracks and formats speakers pick from
`set_rooms_and_tracks { event_id, tracks?, formats? }` replaces the whole list. Keep an item by passing its `id` with its name (a new name renames it); add one with a name only; anything left out is removed. Read the current lists from `get_sessions_event` first. **Pause:** show the full new list and what will be removed. If a session still uses one, nothing in that list changes and you are told which.

### 6. Open the call
**Pause:** show the final title, welcome text, closing date and the questions in order. Ask "Open the call for speakers? It becomes public." On yes:
`manage_call_for_speakers { action: "open", event_id, asked }` (pass the person's words in `asked`). It answers `needs_approval`: say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Once a person approves, `get_sessions_event` shows it open with the link to share.

### 7. Watch submissions come in
- `get_sessions_home {}` for the counts (submitted, undecided, accepted, declined).
- `list_submissions { event_id, view: "submissions", status? }` for what came through the call. `status: "pending"` keeps only the undecided ones. Lead with how many and what is new since the person last asked: titles, speakers, tracks.
- To record a proposal that arrived by email: **Pause:** show title, description and speakers (each with an email). On yes: `manage_program_session { action: "add", event_id, title, description?, speakers?, as_submission: true }`. Send each speaker as `first_name`, `last_name`, `email` and `job_title` only: Sessionboard refuses `company` here, so leave it out (add the company afterwards on the contact). It lands undecided with the rest.
- Deciding is the `review-and-decide-submissions` skill.

### 8. Close the call
**Pause:** "Close the call now? Submissions already in stay." On yes: `manage_call_for_speakers { action: "close", event_id }`.

## When something goes wrong

- 403 "… is not part of this Sessions plan" (`enterprise_only`): the plan does not include it (a second form, conditional questions, more questions of its own, another event this year). Nothing changed. A person with admin rights chooses a bigger plan in Sessions → Plan and billing. Do not work around it.
- `trial_ended` / `plan_ended`: the workspace is read-only. Everything can still be read; a person chooses a plan in Sessionboard.
- 403 "Forbidden … needs the read:sessions scope …": missing scope or not an organization admin. Reconnect the connector if scopes were added later. A 403 naming a limited connection: it needs an organization-wide one.
- 404: check the event id with `get_sessions_home`. 401 "Not signed in": reconnect the connector.
- 409 `in_use`: a session still uses that track or format. Move those sessions first, then try again.
- "That question is already on the call." / "field_ids must list every question in the … group exactly once": read `get_call_questions` again and fix the call.

## What this skill does not do

- Conditional questions, a second form, submission fees, file-upload questions of the event's own, or committee Review: the Sessionboard platform.
- No reminder emails to speakers, no speaker portal, and no notification when a submission arrives: you read the list when asked.
- No CSV export through the connector (export from the Sessions pages).
- Cannot change the call's images or branding.

## Tools used

- `get_sessions_home` — the plan, Sessions events, counts, whether each call is open (read)
- `find_event` — find a full-platform event by name (read)
- `list_events` — every event in the organization (read)
- `get_sessions_event` — the call's text, closing date, public link, tracks, formats (read)
- `manage_sessions_event` — create an event or change its details and speaker language (write)
- `manage_call_for_speakers` — change the call's text or closing date, close it, or open it (write; opening waits in Sessionboard)
- `get_call_questions` — the questions, catalog, answered counts and plan limit (read)
- `manage_call_questions` — add, create, remove, require or reorder questions (write, live at once)
- `set_rooms_and_tracks` — the full track and format lists speakers pick from (write)
- `list_submissions` — what came through the call, with decisions (read)
- `manage_program_session` — enter a submission for someone (write)

skills.instructions:
# Run the Awards review

The person gets their Reviewers invited and assigned, scoring chased until it is done, a clear view of how Submissions score, and the Winners and Finalists announced once they have picked them in Sessionboard. It works the same for a self-serve Awards workspace and a full-platform organization. Self-serve Awards has one review Round per program; more Rounds are Enterprise Awards. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to run the review of an Awards program - invite Reviewers, give every Submission its Reviewers, remind Reviewers who have scorecards to finish, see how scoring is going and how Submissions stand, and announce the Winners and Finalists once a person has picked them. Triggers on "invite these people as Reviewers", "assign the nominations to Reviewers", "three Reviewers per Submission", "who hasn't finished scoring?", "remind the Reviewers", "how is the review going?", "show me the top-scored nominations", "compare the finalists", "hide nominee names from Reviewers", "announce the winners", "send the winner emails".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person, with an organization-wide connection (a key restricted to events is refused).
- Reads need `read:awards`; invites, assignments, reminders and announcements need `write:awards`.
- Sessionboard checks `ORG.AWARDS.READ` to read and `ORG.AWARDS.UPDATE` plus being a manager of the program to change it. Lists and totals only show programs the person manages or can see.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write or send.** Before `invite_awards_reviewers`, `assign_awards_reviews`, `update_awards_program`, `remind_awards` with `preview: false` or `announce_awards_winners`, show exactly what will happen (names and emails, how many Reviewers per Submission, who gets which email) and get a clear yes in this conversation. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads need no confirmation.
- **Some actions wait for a person in Sessionboard.** Inviting Reviewers, sending reminders and announcing answer `needs_approval` with a URL. Say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Do not call it again for the same program.
- **Choosing Winners is a person's job in Sessionboard** (Awards → the program → Winners). There is no tool for it and Sessionboard refuses an assistant. You may help compare Submissions with their scores; never say who won, and never mark anyone.
- Pass the person's request in their own words as `asked` on the invite, reminder and announcement.
- Words: Reviewer, Round, Scorecard, Submission (nomination), Nominee, Winner, Finalist. Never "judge", "jury", "entry" or "evaluation".

## The workflow

1. **Find the program.** `list_awards_programs { offset? }` for status (draft, open, reviewing, closed), Round dates and counts. Then `get_awards_program { program_id, submissions_offset? }`: the program under `program` (status, `counts.submitted`), and beside it at the top level the Submissions with average scores (50 at a time), `review.reviewers` (each with `assigned`, `done` and `not_started`), the Scorecard and the Winner types.
2. **Invite Reviewers.** Collect each Reviewer's email and ask for their first and last name too, since the invitation greets them by name; if the person does not have names, invite by email alone (up to 50 per call). Each gets an account and an invitation email to the review portal.
   **Pause:** list every name and email. Ask "Send these invitations?"
   On yes: `invite_awards_reviewers { program_id, reviewers, asked? }`. It answers `needs_approval`: give the URL and stop. The invitations go once a person approves.
3. **Blind review (optional).** If the person wants Reviewers not to see nominator or Nominee names:
   **Pause:** "Turn on blind review for <program>?"
   `update_awards_program { program_id, blind_review: true }`.
4. **Assign reviews.** It spreads submitted Submissions across the Reviewers, least busy first. Default 3 Reviewers per Submission. It keeps every assignment already made and only fills gaps, and it emails no one: Reviewers see their list in the review portal.
   - Read `get_awards_program` first. When `review.reviewers` is empty (invitations still waiting for an OK in Sessionboard, or none sent) or `counts.submitted` is 0 (a draft, or nominations still open with nothing submitted), there is nothing to assign yet: say which, and offer to assign once Reviewers are on the program and Submissions are in, usually when nominations close and the review Round starts. Calling again later only fills gaps.
   - Each Submission can get at most as many Reviewers as the program has. With fewer Reviewers than `per_submission` (2 Reviewers and the default 3), say so and propose `per_submission` equal to the Reviewer count, or inviting more Reviewers first.
   **Pause:** say how many Submissions and Reviewers there are and how many Reviewers each Submission gets. Ask for a yes.
   `assign_awards_reviews { program_id, per_submission? }`.
5. **Chase unfinished scorecards** (while the review Round is open). `remind_awards { program_id, audience: "reviewers", preview: true }` lists who would get it and who is skipped (nobody gets the same reminder twice in 24 hours). Nothing is sent.
   **Pause:** show the count, the names and who is skipped. Ask "Send this reminder?"
   On yes: `remind_awards { program_id, audience: "reviewers", preview: false, asked? }`. It answers `needs_approval`: give the URL and stop.
6. **Read how it is going.** `get_awards_results` for every program: Submissions submitted and still in draft, Reviewers, Scorecards filled in, Winners and the completion rate. `get_awards_program` for one program's Reviewer progress and Submissions by average score. Present scores as information for the person's decision, not a recommendation of Winners.
7. **Hand the choice to the person.** When scoring is done, say: "Pick the Winners and Finalists in Sessionboard: Awards → <program> → Winners." Do not continue until they say they have.
8. **Announce.** Check `get_awards_program` shows Winners. Whoever submitted each Winner's and Finalist's nomination (the Nominee, when people nominate themselves) gets the news by email; everyone else who submitted gets a thank-you unless `notify_others` is false. It is sent once per program.
   **Pause:** say which program, how many Winners and Finalists, whether the thank-you goes out, and any `note` line. Ask "Announce now?"
   On yes: `announce_awards_winners { program_id, note?, notify_others?, asked? }`. It answers `needs_approval`: give the URL and stop.

## When something goes wrong

- **403 "Forbidden … needs the read:awards scope … and a user who can manage Awards"**: missing scope, or the person is not a manager of this program. They reconnect, or ask an admin.
- **403 with `plan_ended` / `trial_ended`** in the message: the self-serve plan is read-only. A person chooses a plan in Sessionboard (Awards → Plan and billing).
- **`choose_plan`** on announce: the organization is past the trial's 50 nominations (counted across all its programs). A person chooses a plan in Sessionboard; nothing was sent; nominations still come in.
- **`enterprise_only`** (`review_rounds`): a second review Round is Enterprise Awards. An admin upgrades in Sessionboard (Awards → Enterprise). Nothing changed.
- **"A person does this in Sessionboard, not an assistant."** (`HUMAN_ONLY`): say so and point to the page.
- **Announce errors mentioning `no_winners` or `reviews_incomplete`**: no Winners are picked yet, or scorecards are unfinished. Say which, and offer step 5 or step 7.
- **Reminder errors mentioning `review_not_open` / `review_closed` / `no_site`**: the review Round is not open now, or the program is not on an Awards Site. Say so.
- **404**: check the id with `list_awards_programs`.
- **429 "Too many requests"**: Sessionboard is rate-limiting this connection. Nothing changed. Wait a minute and retry once; if it happens again, tell the person and try later.

## What this skill does not do

- Pick, change or remove Winners or Finalists. A person does that in Sessionboard.
- Preview exactly who gets the announcement email before asking. Say who receives it in general terms instead.
- Remove a Reviewer, move an assignment from one Reviewer to another, or set Reviewer tags.
- Show one Reviewer's individual scorecard answers.
- Run more than one review Round, public voting or a Call for Reviewers.
- Report the delivery progress of a reminder or announcement after it is sent.

skills.instructions:
# Sell courses and report credits

The person gets their courses priced, discounted and described on their Learning Site, a clear view of sales, and their earned credit checked, exported or sent to CE Broker. Every change waits for their OK in Sessionboard. Sessionboard Learning is an LMS; selling and credit reporting are capabilities in it. It works the same for a self-serve Learning workspace and a full-platform organization with the Learning module. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to sell courses on their Learning Site and report earned credit to CE Broker - set a course's price and member price, make or stop coupons, write the course page description, require watching before a step counts, see sales and whether card payments are on, mark members and keep learners' license numbers, refund an order or end access, and check, export or send the CE Broker report. Triggers on "charge $49 for this course, free for members", "make a 20% off coupon", "stop the SPRING coupon", "write a description for the course page", "require watching 80%", "how are course sales?", "can learners pay by card yet?", "refund this order", "remove their access", "export my CE Broker report", "report credits to CE Broker", "set up CE Broker".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person.
- Reads need `read:learning`; changes need `write:learning`.
- Sessionboard checks the Learning module and the Lessons permissions (`ORG.LESSONS.READ` / `ORG.LESSONS.UPDATE`). Refunds and removing access also need the permission that manages plan and billing, or an organization admin.
- **CE Broker runs in practice mode** (`mode: "mock"`) until a real CE Broker provider account is connected. In practice mode nothing leaves Sessionboard and nothing is recorded as reported. Say so every time.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write or send.** Before any price, coupon, description, watch requirement, learner profile, CE Broker setup, CE Broker send, refund or access change, show exactly what will change (course, amounts in dollars and cents, coupon code and dates, the learner, the order and amount) and get a clear yes in this conversation. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads and dry runs need no confirmation.
- **Every write waits for a person in Sessionboard.** From an assistant each one answers `needs_approval` with a URL. Say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Do not call it again.
- **Refunds only on an explicit request for that order.** Money goes back to a card. Name the learner, course, amount and whether access ends, and get a yes for that exact order.
- **Never ask for payment gateway keys or the CE Broker upload key.** A person enters them in Sessionboard.
- **Never call practice-mode results "reported".** `mode: "mock"` means rows were checked, nothing was sent.
- Amounts are in cents: 4900 = $49, 0 = free. Say dollars to the person.
- Words: Learning, course, learner, member, credit, coupon. Never "Lessons & Credits".

## The workflow

1. **Where things stand.** `read_learning_workspace { view: "courses" }` lists courses with their price. `read_course_selling { view: "payments" }` says whether card payments are on. If not, learners can get a course only with a 100% coupon or a $0 member price; a person connects a payment gateway in Sessionboard (Site › Selling › Get paid).
2. **Price a course.**
   **Pause:** "Set <course> to $<price>, members $<member price>, in <currency>?"
   `set_course_price { course_id, amount_cents, member_amount_cents?, currency? }` (USD default; CAD, EUR, GBP, AUD). Members are learners marked members or linked to the association management system. Coupons come off after the member price.
3. **Coupons.** `read_course_selling { view: "coupons", archived? }` shows each code, amount, courses, dates, uses and state.
   **Pause:** show the code, percent or amount off, which courses (empty = every course), start and end, and use limit.
   Create: `manage_coupon { action: "create", code, kind: "percent" | "amount", amount, currency?, course_ids?, starts_at?, ends_at?, max_uses? }`. Change: `{ action: "update", coupon_id, ... }`. Stop now: `{ action: "archive", coupon_id }`. Bring back: `{ action: "restore", coupon_id }`.
4. **The course page.** `read_course_page { course_id }` returns the description, or `summary_draft` (a starting point, not public) and what learners will learn.
   **Pause:** show the exact text (up to 1,000 characters).
   `set_course_description { course_id, summary }` (`""` removes it).
5. **Require watching** (off by default). A video step counts only after the learner played at least `percent` of it (10–100, skipping ahead does not count).
   **Pause:** "Require <n>% watched on every video in <course>?"
   `set_course_watch_requirement { course_id, percent }` (`null` turns it off).
6. **Sales.** `read_course_selling { view: "sales" }`: orders with learner, course, amount paid, list and member price, coupon, and totals per currency.
7. **Members and licenses.** Find the learner with `read_learners { action: "find", q }`.
   **Pause:** show the change.
   `update_learner_profile { learner_id, member?, license_number?, license_state?, license_profession? }` (two-letter state; profession code like RN).
8. **Refund or end access** (only when asked for a specific order). Find it in `read_course_selling { view: "sales" }` (status paid, amount above 0).
   **Pause:** "Refund <learner>'s <course> order of $<amount> in full to their card? They keep the course unless you want access removed."
   `refund_course_order { order_id, remove_access? }`. For an order that charged nothing, or after a refund made in the gateway: `remove_course_access { order_id }` (progress and credit stay on record).
9. **CE Broker report.** `read_ce_broker_report`: setup, `mode`, credited courses with CE Broker course numbers, and every credit's status (ready, missing, missing_license, failed, reported). Say what is missing in words.
   - **Set up** (after a yes): `set_up_ce_broker { provider_number?, default_profession?, course_numbers? }` (`course_numbers` maps a course id to its CE Broker number; `null` removes one).
   - **Export** (every plan): `export_ce_broker_report { format? }`. `xml` (default) is CE Broker's upload format with the ready rows; `csv` lists every row with its status. Hand over the file and say the person uploads the XML in CE Broker's provider portal, or downloads the same file under Credits › CE Broker reporting.
   - **Send** (Enterprise only): first `report_to_ce_broker { dry_run: true }` and say how many would go.
     **Pause:** "Send <n> learners' names and license numbers to CE Broker?" (In practice mode: "This is practice; nothing will leave Sessionboard.")
     On yes: `report_to_ce_broker { dry_run: false }`. It answers `needs_approval`: give the URL and stop. After a person approves, report `sent`, `accepted` and each `rejected` row with its message.

## When something goes wrong

- **403 "Forbidden … needs the read:learning / write:learning scopes … and a user with the Lessons permission"**: the person reconnects or asks an admin.
- **403 on a refund or removing access**: the person lacks the plan-and-billing permission. Say so; an organization admin can do it.
- **403 `enterprise_only` from `report_to_ce_broker`**: sending is Sessionboard Enterprise. Use `export_ce_broker_report` and hand over the file. Nothing changed.
- **400 from `refund_course_order`**: the order charged nothing (use `remove_course_access`) or is already refunded.
- **400 from `export_ce_broker_report`**: nothing is ready or there is no provider number. Say which.
- **"code, kind and amount are required" / "coupon_id is required"**: supply them; nothing changed.
- **404**: check ids with `read_learning_workspace { view: "courses" }` or `read_course_selling`.

## What this skill does not do

- Connect a payment gateway or enter any key. A person does that in Sessionboard.
- Make a partial refund. Refunds are in full.
- Set or grant credit, or edit a course's credit amount.
- Report to CE Broker for real while the organization has no real CE Broker provider account (practice mode only).
- Report to boards other than CE Broker (for example PARS or CPE Monitor).
- Upload a cover image for the course page.

## Tools used

- `read_learning_workspace` — courses with their prices (read)
- `read_course_selling` — coupons, sales and payment status (read)
- `set_course_price` — a course's price and member price; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `manage_coupon` — create, update, stop or restore a coupon; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `read_course_page` — a course's public page and draft description (read)
- `set_course_description` — the description on the course page; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `set_course_watch_requirement` — require watching before a step counts; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `read_learners` — find a learner (read)
- `update_learner_profile` — member status and license details; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `refund_course_order` — refund a paid order in full; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `remove_course_access` — end a buyer's access; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `read_ce_broker_report` — setup, mode and every credit's reporting status (read)
- `set_up_ce_broker` — provider number, default profession, course numbers; waits for a person's OK (write)
- `export_ce_broker_report` — the roster file as XML or CSV (read)
- `report_to_ce_broker` — dry run, then send ready credit; Enterprise only, waits for a person's OK (sends)

skills.starterPrompt:

Use my Sessionboard connector. Goal: A sponsor's counts-only report and a safe link to hand it over, plus, when you choose, a private link to the people who opted in to hear from sponsors.

skills.instructions:
# Send a sponsor their results

The person gets a sponsor's report from what Sessionboard already tracks, and a safe way to hand it over: a read-only link to the counts, and, when they choose, a private link to the people who opted in to hear from sponsors. It works for any organization with Sessionboard Marketing, a Marketing workspace or a full-platform account, with the same tools. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

**Sponsors get aggregates, never attendee names.** The sponsor report is counts only. The only people a sponsor can ever see are those who subscribed to hear from sponsors, through `share_with_sponsor`, and only after a person approves it in Sessionboard.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to show a sponsor what their sponsorship delivered — pick the sponsor, read their counts-only report (session views and watches, attendance, questions, clips, posts, link clicks, credited registrations, app placement views and taps, booth leads), send them a read-only link to it, give them a private link to the people who opted in to hear from sponsors, see who opened the links, and stop a link working. Triggers on "how did Acme's sponsorship do?", "send Acme their report", "make a sponsor report for Globex", "share the results with our sponsor", "give Acme the opted-in list", "which sponsor links were opened?", "revoke Acme's link", "kill that sponsor link".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person.
- Scopes: `read:marketing` to read reports and links; `write:marketing` to make or revoke a link. Adding a sponsor to an event also needs `write:sponsors`.
- Sessionboard checks that the person belongs to the organization. Reading results and making a results link need an org **Contacts** permission (read, update or manage). Making or revoking a private sponsor link needs an org admin. A connection limited to particular events cannot read an org-wide report.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write or share.** Before `share_results`, `share_with_sponsor`, `revoke_sponsor_share` or `manage_sponsor`, say exactly what happens: which sponsor, which report or audience, how many people (a count), how long the link works. Get a clear yes in this conversation. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads need no confirmation.
- **Some actions wait for a person in Sessionboard.** `share_results` and `share_with_sponsor` from an assistant can answer `needs_approval` with a URL. Tell the person "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop. Do not call it again.
- **Pass `asked`** (the person's request in their own words, one sentence) on `share_results`, `share_with_sponsor` and `revoke_sponsor_share`, so the approval in Sessionboard shows what they asked for.
- **Never put a name in front of a sponsor.** Read the report with `scope: "sponsor"` only. Never paste rows from an event or org report (people, posts by attendees) into anything meant for the sponsor.
- **A link can be opened by anyone who has it.** Say so before making one. A results link works 30 days unless `days` says otherwise.
- **Never invent a number.** Every figure you state is in the report. Credited registrations are shared across touches over 90 days (40% first, 40% last, 20% between), so they can be fractions; say "credited", never "brought".
- Words: **sponsor** (never "partner"), **Advocacy** for sharing, **Surveys** for attendee feedback. Never name the in-product assistant or internal engines.

## The workflow

1. **Pick the sponsor.** `list_report_sponsors { q? }` (up to 50; sponsors on the organization's events and company records). If several match, show the names and ask which. It returns names only: for "our top sponsor", ask the person which one, or read two or three reports (step 2) and compare them before choosing.
   - Not listed because they are not on the event yet: ask, then `manage_sponsor { action: "create", event_id, name, level?, website?, contact_email?, description? }`. Sessions must still be tagged with the sponsor in Sessionboard before the report has numbers.
2. **Read the report.** `get_results { scope: "sponsor", sponsor_id, event_id?, from?, to? }`. `event_id` narrows to one event; `from` / `to` are `YYYY-MM-DD`. Lead with the answer, then the counts: their sessions' views, watches and attendance, questions, clips, posts, link clicks and credited registrations, app placement views and taps, and booth leads. If a list says `truncated`, say the totals still cover everything.
3. **Explain it if asked.** `explain_results { scope: "sponsor", sponsor_id, event_id? }`: use its `headline`, `worked`, `did_not` and `next_moves`. Anything you add must come from its `facts` or the report.
4. **Send the report.**
   **Before you offer a link:** if every count in the report is zero, do not share it. Say so: usually no sessions, clips or placements are tagged with this sponsor yet. Offer to look at what to tag instead.

   **Pause:** "Make a read-only link to Acme's sponsor report (counts only, no attendee names) that anyone with it can open for 30 days?"
   On yes: `share_results { scope: "sponsor", sponsor_id, event_id?, from?, to?, title?, days?, asked }`. Give the `url` (it is returned once) and `expires_at`. If it answers `needs_approval`, say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop.
5. **Give the sponsor the opted-in list (optional, only when asked).** First count who would be on it, without saving: `build_audience { definition: { roles, eventId?, attended? } }` (roles: speaker, attendee, contact, visitor). Only people who opted in to hear from sponsors appear on the sponsor's list; counts under 10 show as "Fewer than 10" on the sponsor's page.
   **Pause:** "Create a private link for Acme to the attendees of Summit 2027 who opted in to hear from sponsors, for 30 days? They see counts, a profile of the audience and their report totals, and can download only the opted-in people."
   On yes: `share_with_sponsor { sponsor_account_id, definition: { roles?, event_id?, attended? }, audience_name?, days?, asked }`. `sponsor_account_id` is the sponsor's id from `list_report_sponsors`; use `sponsor_name` only for a sponsor with no record. A saved audience can go in as `audience_id` instead of `definition`. It answers `needs_approval`: say "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop.
6. **See what was opened.** `list_sponsor_shares {}`: each link's sponsor, audience, created, expires, active, views and downloads.
7. **Stop a link.**
   **Pause:** "Stop Acme's link now? Views and downloads so far stay on record."
   `revoke_sponsor_share { share_id, asked }`. A results link from `share_results` is revoked by the person in Results in Sessionboard.

## When something goes wrong

- **`needs_approval`**: not an error. "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>"; do not call again.
- **403 "This token cannot use Marketing"**: the connection lacks `read:marketing` / `write:marketing`, or the person is not an org admin (for sponsor links). Reports need a connection not limited to particular events.
- **409**: the link or report changed; read it again before retrying.
- **400 / 422 "Invalid request"**: say the message; usually a missing `sponsor_id` with `scope: "sponsor"`, or neither a sponsor nor an audience on `share_with_sponsor`.
- **404 "Not found"**: check the sponsor with `list_report_sponsors` and the link with `list_sponsor_shares`.

## What this skill does not do

- No sponsor report for exhibitors, and no PDF or CSV export of the report from here (the Results page in Sessionboard has Export CSV).
- It cannot list or revoke results links; a person revokes those in Results.
- It cannot email the link to the sponsor; the person sends it.
- It cannot tag sessions with a sponsor, or change an existing event sponsor's details; do those in Sessionboard.
- No revenue share or sponsored-reach packages.

## Tools used

- `list_report_sponsors` — pick the sponsor (read)
- `manage_sponsor` — add a missing sponsor to an event (write)
- `get_results` — the sponsor's counts-only report with `scope: "sponsor"` (read)
- `explain_results` — what worked, in plain words (read)
- `share_results` — a read-only link to the report; may wait for approval (write)
- `build_audience` — count who a sponsor link would cover, counts only; used here without `save`, so nothing is stored (write tool, no change)
- `share_with_sponsor` — a private link to the opted-in people; waits for approval (sends)
- `list_sponsor_shares` — sponsor links with views and downloads (read)
- `revoke_sponsor_share` — stop a sponsor link (write)

# Sessionboard Sites by chat

One Site builder serves Learning Sites, Marketing event pages and Awards Sites. These tools edit the same draft the builder in Sessionboard shows, so the person sees your edits appear in an open builder, and you read theirs.

## When to use

Build and edit a Sessionboard Site (Learning, Marketing or Awards) by chat — pages, blocks, menu, light/dark and Brand Kit, preview as a role on a device, see what changes, publish on the person's OK, restore an earlier version.

## The loop

1. **Find the Site**: `list_sites` (filter by `product`). If there is none, `make_site`: from the org's own data (`product`), from a page (`url` → `source_page`), or for an event (`event_id`, Marketing).
2. **Read it**: `get_site`. Note `revision`, the page `ref`s, block `id`s, `roles` and `block_catalog` (each kind's config schema and an example).
3. **Edit the draft**: `edit_site { site_id, base_revision, ops }`. Each op is an object whose `op` key names it. Batch related changes into one call. On a 409, read again and redo. **Pause:** say what you will add or change, then edit on their yes (it changes the draft only; nothing goes live).
   - "Add an FAQ about parking" → `ops: [{ op: "block.add", block: { kind: "faq", config: { heading: "Parking", items: [{ question, answer }] } } }]`
   - "Make the hero shorter" → `ops: [{ op: "block.update", block: { id, config: { intro: "…" } } }]` (config merges)
   - "Add a Parking page and put it in the menu" → `{ op: "page.add", … }`, then after publishing `{ op: "nav.set", … }` (a menu item needs a published page id; until then the menu follows the pages).
   - "Dark mode, our green" → `ops: [{ op: "theme.set", theme: { mode: "dark", primary: "#14653A" } }]`
4. **Show it**: `preview_site` for the role and device that matter ("as a learner on a phone") and give the person `preview_url`; `get_site_diff` for `summary`.
5. **Publish only on their OK**: `publish_site { revision, confirmed: true }` with the revision of the diff they approved. From a connected assistant this answers *needs_approval*: tell them "Waiting for your OK in Sessionboard: <url>" and stop.
6. **Undo**: `list_site_versions` → `restore_site_version` (into the draft) → show the diff → publish on their OK.

## Rules

- Never publish without an explicit OK in this conversation. Never infer it.
- Speakers, dates, places and course lists come from Sessionboard data. Do not type them into text blocks yourself. Details the person gives you in this conversation ("parking is in Lot B") are fine to write; ask for any you would otherwise have to guess.
- Marketing event pages are one page (`page: "home"`) and keep their hero and Register blocks.
- Words: Review (Reviewer, Round), never "judge" or "evaluation"; Nominee for people who submit to Awards.

## Tools used

- `edit_site` — Edit Site draft (write)
- `get_site` — Get Site (read)
- `get_site_diff` — What would change (read)
- `list_site_versions` — List Site versions (read)
- `list_sites` — List Sites (read)
- `make_site` — Make a Site (write)
- `preview_site` — Preview Site (read)
- `publish_site` — Publish Site (write)

skills.instructions:
# Keep your people and companies tidy

The person gets a clean People list in Sessionboard CRM: the right names and titles, the right tags, people linked to the companies they work at, new lists brought in without duplicates, and an export when they need one. It works the same for a self-serve CRM workspace and a full-platform organization. Plan limits and role permissions are enforced by Sessionboard, not by you.

Two records, never one: a **person** (People, one per email) and a **Contact** (the record behind a speaker or a company's person, which the pipeline and contracts use) stay separate and are linked by email. Never tell the person they are the same record or that one was merged into the other. In the app, companies are shown as **Groups** (companies, sponsors, exhibitors, chapters); the tools say `company`.

## When to use

Use this when someone wants to clean up the people and companies (Groups) in Sessionboard CRM — find someone, fix a name or title, tag people as speakers, members, customers or prospects, tag companies as sponsors or exhibitors, link people to the company they work at, bring in a spreadsheet or a connected CRM's contacts with a preview first, export a list, or delete records. Triggers on "clean up my contacts", "find everyone at Acme", "tag these 40 people as speakers", "mark Acme as a sponsor", "link Dana to Acme", "import this spreadsheet", "bring in our HubSpot contacts", "who is a member?", "export our speakers", "fix Dana's title", "delete these duplicates".

## Before you start

- The Sessionboard connector is signed in with OAuth as the person.
- Scopes: `read:crm` to read, discover, preview and export; `write:crm` to change anything. They are preview scopes, so they must be named explicitly when the connector or key is set up. Adding a sponsor or exhibitor to an event's own list also needs `write:sponsors` / `write:exhibitors`.
- Sessionboard checks the person's org **Contacts** permissions, the same as the Contacts pages: READ to look, UPDATE to add, edit, tag, link or import, DELETE to delete, EXPORT to export. Bringing in an event platform's attendees needs an org admin. A role limited to some portfolios is refused here; that person uses Contacts in Sessionboard.

## Guardrails (read first)

- **Confirm before every write.** Before any tool that creates, changes or deletes, show exactly what will change (names, emails, tags, counts, the company) and get a clear yes in this conversation. Never infer a yes from an earlier answer or a plan. Reads need no confirmation.
- **Updates replace lists.** On `manage_crm_person` update, `roles` and `company_ids` replace the whole list; on `manage_crm_company` update, `tags` replaces. To add or remove one tag on many records use `tag_crm_people` / `tag_crm_companies`, which leave other tags alone. Read the record first and show before and after.
- **Tags have side effects; say them.** Tagging someone `speaker` makes them a Contact. `member` sets their membership. `customer` or `prospect` records a lifecycle change. Linking a person to a company makes them a Contact of that company. A `sponsor` or `exhibitor` tag on a company also shows it on the platform's sponsor or exhibitor pages.
- **Deletes need `confirmed: true`,** passed only after the person said yes to the named list. Stored people are free (the plan counts active contacts only), so never suggest deleting to save money. Deleting a person keeps their Contact, contracts and pipeline entries; deleted companies go to the platform's Trash and their people stay.
- **Only standard fields.** Name, title, email, company, website and tags. Custom fields are part of the Sessionboard platform (an upgrade); say so instead of guessing a field.
- **Never ask for app keys.** Connecting a CRM, AMS or event platform is done by the person in Sessionboard CRM → Connections.
- Nothing here emails anyone. Words: say **prospect** (never "lead"), **sponsor** (never "partner"), **Groups** for companies in the app. Never name the in-product assistant or internal engines.

## The workflow

1. **Get the lay of the land.** `get_crm_home {}`: counts per tag, active contacts used against the plan's limit, setup steps, the newest people.
2. **Find people.** `find_crm_people { q?, roles?, all_roles?, company_id?, member?, lifecycle?, in_pipeline?, attended?, event_id?, active?, linked?, warm?, sort?, page?, per_page? }`. `roles` matches any of the tags; add `all_roles: true` for all of them. Use `facets` to give counts. One person: `get_crm_person { key }` (CRM view, signals timeline, linked Contact).
   - `q` matches name, email and the linked company, so `q: "acme.com"` finds people by their email domain. `company_id` finds only people already linked to that company: before anyone is linked, "everyone at Acme" is found by the email domain, not by the company.
   - Keys can change: once a person becomes a Contact (a `speaker` tag, a company link) their key goes from `p_…` to `c_…`. Old keys still resolve in `get_crm_person`, but read the people again before a follow-up write and use the keys you get back.
   - **Nothing found:** when the named company or its people are not here, say so plainly. Offer to look by email domain (`find_crm_people { q: "<domain>" }`), to create the company (step 5), and, if people turn up by domain, to create the company and link them (step 7). Do not create a company unless the person says yes.
3. **Find companies.** `find_crm_companies { q?, tags?, sort?, page?, per_page? }`, or `find_crm_companies { company_id }` for one company with its people, contracts and pipeline.
4. **Fix a person.** `manage_crm_person { action: "update", key, first_name?, last_name?, title?, roles?, company_ids? }`. Add someone new: `manage_crm_person { action: "create", email, first_name?, last_name?, title?, company?, company_id?, roles? }`. An email already here is not added twice.
   **Pause:** show the current record and the change, field by field; ask "Save this?"
5. **Fix a company.** `manage_crm_company { action: "update", company_id, name?, website?, tags? }`, or `action: "create"` with `name`. A name already here is not added twice.
   **Pause:** show the current company (or the new one) and the change; ask "Save this?"
6. **Tag in bulk.** `tag_crm_people { keys, add?, remove? }` (up to 500; `contacts_created` says how many became Contacts through `speaker`). `tag_crm_companies { company_ids, add?, remove? }` (sponsor, exhibitor; up to 500).
   **Pause:** "Tag 40 people as speaker? That also makes them Contacts." Name the count and a few names.
7. **Link people to a company.** `link_crm_company_people { action: "link", company_id, keys? }`, or someone new with `email, first_name?, last_name?, title?`. Remove one: `link_crm_company_people { action: "unlink", company_id, keys: [one key] }`; the person stays.
   **Pause:** "Link these 5 people to Acme? Each becomes a Contact of Acme." Name the people and the company.
   Show before and after from the person's `companies` list (a link shows there; the `company` text field can stay empty). Read the people again afterwards: their keys may now start with `c_`.
8. **The organization's own lists.** `list_crm_tags {}` shows them with counts; `manage_crm_tag { action: "create" | "rename" | "delete", tag_id?, name? }`. Deleting a list keeps every Contact on it.
9. **Import a spreadsheet.** Read the file the person shared and turn each row into `{ email, first_name?, last_name?, company?, title?, roles? }` (or `{ name, website?, tags? }` with `target: "companies"`).
   - `import_crm_people { action: "preview", target?, rows }` writes nothing. Report `total`, `new`, `existing`, `duplicates_in_file` and each `invalid` line with its reason.
   - **Pause:** "40 new, 12 already here, 3 invalid (lines 7, 19, 33: no email). Import the 40 new? Fill in details for the 12 already here?" Only pass `update_existing: true` if they say yes to that part.
   - `import_crm_people { action: "import", target?, rows, update_existing? }` with only the rows they agreed to. If the answer has `stopped_at_row`, say which rows went in and which did not.
10. **Bring people in from a connected app.** `list_crm_sources {}` shows what is connected. `discover_crm_people { app_id, kinds?, default_type? }` reads the app and writes nothing (event platforms: `action: "list_events"` first, then `remote_event_id`). Tell the person what was found ("40 subject-matter experts, 12 new"), then preview and import as in step 9 with `source: app_id`.
    An event platform's attendees: tell the person how many `discover_crm_people` found and ask, then `start_crm_attendee_sync { app_id, remote_event_id, event_id? }`. They land in People, never as Contacts. Nothing is written to the event platform.
11. **Export.** `export_crm_contacts { q?, type?, tag_id?, source?, event_id?, active? }` returns the Contacts as CSV, up to 1,000 rows. If `truncated`, say the full list exports from the Contacts page in Sessionboard CRM (up to 25,000).
12. **Delete.** Name every record first. **Pause:** "Delete these 3 people? Their Contacts, contracts and pipeline entries stay." Then `delete_crm_people { keys, confirmed: true }` or `delete_crm_companies { company_ids, confirmed: true }`.
13. **Put a company on an event's sponsor or exhibitor list.** Ask first, then `manage_sponsor { action: "create", event_id, name, level?, website?, contact_email?, description? }` or `manage_exhibitor { action: "create", event_id, name, booth_number?, website?, contact_email?, description? }`.

## When something goes wrong

- **403 "This connection cannot use Sessionboard CRM"**: the connector lacks `read:crm` / `write:crm`, or the person's role lacks the Contacts permission. If scopes were added after connecting, disconnect and reconnect. A portfolio-limited role is told to use Contacts in Sessionboard.
- **Read-only** (`trial_ended`, `plan_ended`, `paused`, `payment_due`, `read_only`): everything can still be read; a person with admin rights chooses a plan or updates billing in CRM → Plan and billing. Nothing was changed.
- **`exists`**: the email or company name is already here; nothing was added. Offer an update instead.
- **`platform_customer`**: the organization's contacts live in the platform's CRM, not the self-serve workspace.
- **404**: check keys with `find_crm_people`, company ids with `find_crm_companies`, tag ids with `list_crm_tags`, app ids with `list_crm_sources`.
- **`sync_disabled`** on keeping a source in sync: not turned on for this organization; people can still be brought in once.

## What this skill does not do

- It cannot add a Contact to one of the organization's own lists (tags from `list_crm_tags`); that is done in Sessionboard.
- No People or Groups export (only the Contacts export, 1,000 rows); no custom fields; no notes on a person.
- It cannot connect an app or change an existing event sponsor's or exhibitor's details (an update needs a version these tools do not read); do those in Sessionboard.
- It does not merge two people into one.

## Tools used

- `get_crm_home` — counts, plan meter, setup steps (read)
- `find_crm_people` — search and filter People (read)
- `get_crm_person` — one person with the linked Contact (read)
- `find_crm_companies` — search companies (Groups), or one with its people (read)
- `manage_crm_person` — add or change a person (write)
- `manage_crm_company` — add or change a company (write)
- `tag_crm_people` — add or remove person tags in bulk (write)
- `tag_crm_companies` — add or remove sponsor / exhibitor tags in bulk (write)
- `link_crm_company_people` — link or unlink people and a company (write)
- `list_crm_tags` — the organization's lists with counts (read)
- `manage_crm_tag` — create, rename or delete a list (write)
- `import_crm_people` — preview (read), then import (write)
- `list_crm_sources` — connected CRMs, AMSs and event platforms (read)
- `discover_crm_people` — who a connected app holds, writes nothing (read)
- `start_crm_attendee_sync` — bring an event platform's attendees into People (write)
- `export_crm_contacts` — Contacts as CSV (read)
- `delete_crm_people` — delete people, `confirmed: true` (write)
- `delete_crm_companies` — delete companies to Trash, `confirmed: true` (write)
- `manage_sponsor` — add a sponsor to an event (write)
- `manage_exhibitor` — add an exhibitor to an event (write)
